subject: SCIENCE
title: Materials Can Change
objective: Observe safe examples of changes from heating or cooling.
introduction: Milo watches an ice cube melt in a warm room. What happens to materials when they get hot or cold?

vocabulary.definition: What something is made of, like wood or plastic.
To look closely and notice what happens.

items.prompt: Which statement about heating and cooling is true?

options.text: Heating or cooling can cause physical changes; some are reversible and others are not.

items.explanation: Heating or cooling can change materials, but not every material melts and not every change can be undone — some changes are reversible and others are not.

items.prompt: Which example shows a change caused by heat?

options.text: juice turns into ice pops in the freezer

items.explanation: Ice melts when it gets warm, so heat causes the change. Freezing happens when things get cold.

items.prompt: Which statement is not true?  (in this lesson: Materials Can Change)
items.explanation: Not every material melts — some burn, break, or stay the same. Ice melting and water freezing are real changes.

items.prompt: What happens to ice in a warm room?
items.explanation: A warm room adds heat, so the ice melts into water. Ice does not become metal or turn into fire.

items.prompt: Which change is safe and correct?
items.explanation: Wax softening when warmed is a safe change you can watch. Not every material melts, and touching hot things is unsafe.
